artigo.texto: Hours after the University of Michigan’s Board of Regents voted to approve the University’s and Los Alamos National Laboratory’s planned data center, approximately 350 Ypsilanti Township residents, officials and experts gathered at Eastern Michigan University to oppose the project in a town hall meeting. Attendees condemned the planned data center — which is expected to stretch across 144 acres of the township — and its potential effects on energy costs, water and proximity to indigenous ancestral land. The panelists included Jay Coghlan, executive director of Nuclear Watch New Mexico, a nonprofit that monitors LANL; Michelle Martinez, director of the Tischman Center for Social Justice and the Environment; Ypsilanti Township attorney Doug Winters; Jamie Stuck, the state of Michigan tribal legislative liaison; and state Rep. Jimmy Wilson Jr., D-Ypsilanti. Attendees submitted about 250 written questions to the officials. Coghlan said he believes the choice of the project’s location comes down to one important resource for powering data centers: water. “Why is Los Alamos having the University of Michigan build a data center that’s going to use artificial intelligence to advance new-design nuclear weapons? Why in Ypsilanti?” Coghlan said. “My one-word answer is: water. … (Michigan’s) got water, and we don’t in New Mexico.” Next, Martinez said DTE Energy told shareholders this month it would spend $44 billion over five years to expand its infrastructure, partly to meet data center demand. She said that growth could strain water supplies in two ways: data centers use water on site, and then power plants that supply them, the largest withdrawers of water in Michigan, use even more. “You have this sort of weird trade-off situation with data centers and hyperscale data centers where it’s really difficult to measure,” Martinez said. “And there’s a lot of hydrologists who are increasingly interested in not only what’s being consumed on site, but also what’s being consumed by the power industry.” In response to a question about how to keep the University from buying more land in the township, Wilson Jr. said he plans to reintroduce legislation in January — which he predicts would have bipartisan support — that would require institutions to follow local planning rules when purchasing land outside their home community. The University has indicated that it plans to break ground on the center in late 2027, which it says will expand the University’s computing capabilities and research capacity. Winters argued the project does not serve an educational purpose. “This project is not a University educational purpose,” Winters said. “They have said from day one, this facility is 90% Los Alamos.” Winters then said the township has not set a date to file a legal challenge but does intend to wait until construction begins. “The township board has been very, very adamant that we will use every legal means necessary to stop this,” Winters said. Winters said the Michigan State Historical Preservation Office has advised the University to hire a federal archeologist and contact tribal preservation officers. He told the University the Ypsilanti community’s concerns should be held higher than the potential benefits the data center may provide the University. “You may have extraordinary financial resources,” Winters said. “You may have powerful friends in Lansing and Washington. … but you have come face to face with something your computers cannot calculate, and that is the heart of a community that refuses to be silent.” Ypsilanti Township resident Andy Melichar built a website that compiles residents’ public records requests about the project. He told The Daily he is not broadly opposed to data centers; however, he disagrees with the location of the University’s and Los Alamos’ data center. Experts have criticized the facility for its intended use in nuclear weapons research. “I’m not anti-data center,” Melichar said. “I just am not for putting them where we’re putting them, or for the particular purposes of Los Alamos having nuclear weapons in my backyard. I’m less than a mile away from where they’ll put this in.” Winters told The Daily he believes the project’s most pressing concern for residents is its tie to the federal government, as LANL’s core mission is to solve national security challenges through nuclear weapons design and performance. Michigan’s public universities, including the University, have constitutional autonomy that he believes is being misused in this case. “I think the worst and most pressing issue is the fact that Los Alamos and U-M, has sold its soul to the Department of War,” Winters said. “U-M is a Trojan horse, and they’re abusing their constitutional autonomy by saying, ‘Come on in behind us,’ when … the real dominant partner here is Los Alamos.” Daily News Contributor Eloise Nelson can be reached at eloisen@umich.edu.

artigo.texto: Gelion CEO on Worley partnership, battery scale-up and licensing opportunities Published: 04:50 23 Nov 2026 EST Gelion PLC (AIM:GELN, OTC:GELNF) CEO Matt Wood talked with Proactive about its pre-FEED collaboration with global engineering group Worley to advance production of its nano-encapsulated sulfur (NES) cathode material. Wood explained how Worley's expertise in cathode materials and sulfur processing will help Gelion validate manufacturing processes and develop preliminary designs for a potential pilot plant. The work will cover plant layouts, production requirements, cost estimates and project timelines, helping reduce investment risks ahead of a scale-up decision. The interview also explores growing partnerships across drones, electric vehicles and consumer devices. Wood said existing production capacity can meet near-term demand, but additional volumes will be needed as commercial relationships develop. He outlined the company's strategy of expanding capacity in response to anticipated customer demand, rather than building ahead of the market. Finally, Wood discussed the potential to license NES technology, explaining how the Worley collaboration will help establish the manufacturing processes needed to support future commercial agreements and revenue opportunities. artigo.texto: Romania has added 100 MW of new electricity generation capacity and 36 MW of new energy storage capacity this month, and could reach approximately 1,500 MW of installed energy storage capacity by the end of the year, Energy Minister Dumitru Chisăliță said on Tuesday. “Thanks to intensified monitoring, supervision and discussions with distribution system operators, the energy regulator ANRE and producers, we have managed to bring online 100 MW of new generation capacity and 36 MW of new storage capacity this month,” the minister said at a press conference marking his first month in office, Agerpres reads. He added that the year-end storage target includes projects developed both through investments supported by the Energy Ministry and by private companies. Chisăliță also said the ministry had drawn up competency criteria for appointments to the boards of directors and supervisory boards of state-owned companies, ahead of a wave of board changes expected in 2027, when many current mandates are due to expire. The criteria are intended to improve the selection process and ensure appointments are based on professional qualifications and relevant expertise, he said. The minister also highlighted progress in clearing delayed payments under energy-sector contracts. When he took office, the ministry had 850 contracts with payment delays of up to one year. Payments totalling EUR 200 million were made in November, while a further EUR 280 million is planned for the following month, by the end of the year, with the aim of bringing outstanding payments up to date. Chisăliță said the ministry had also completed the technical documentation for offshore wind energy development, a project that could bring significant additional generation capacity to Romania. He also pointed to efforts to unblock and approve natural gas infrastructure projects, particularly those involving state-owned gas transmission operator Transgaz. Another measure under preparation is an emergency ordinance amending Energy Law 123/2012, currently undergoing public consultation. The proposed changes would require electricity producers to allocate 5% of their output to bilateral contracts and suppliers to purchase 6% of their electricity volumes through such contracts. The measure is intended to increase liquidity and trading activity on the energy market and help reduce electricity prices, the minister said. The Energy Ministry is also preparing changes to the natural gas price framework from April 3, 2027, including an extension and restructuring of the regulated pricing mechanism and the introduction of a one-year transition period towards a fully liberalised gas market. “This draft emergency ordinance is part of the measures we intend to implement over the next three years to ensure a functioning market for both natural gas and electricity,” Chisăliță said. He added that the gas-market proposal was the first of several support schemes and regulatory measures being developed by the ministry, with other initiatives still undergoing consultations and approval procedures with the relevant institutions.

artigo.texto: ORANGE COUNTY, Fla. – The east side of Orange County doesn’t have a skyline. It has smokestacks. The Stanton Energy Center, run by the Orlando Utilities Commission, sits a few miles from the restaurants and homes of Avalon Park. It burns natural gas and coal, and it has solar panels on site. Most people nearby say they rarely think about it. Recommended Videos “From zero to 10?” Avalon Park resident Manouchka said when asked how often she thinks about the plant. “Minus five. It does not register.” But what happens at Stanton is changing, and not in the direction OUC had previously planned. OUC initially planned to put one of Stanton’s two coal-fired units into an extended shutdown at the end of May 2026, part of the utility’s long-running move away from coal. Then the federal government stepped in. On June 4, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright signed an emergency order requiring OUC to keep that coal unit, known as Stanton Unit 1, available to run. The Department of Energy later extended the order through Nov. 30. Click here to see the order. “The Department of Energy said, hey, let’s pump the brakes on this and ensure that we have enough capacity to meet our current needs,” said Orlando Alancastro, OUC’s vice president of transmission. The emergency order points to the growth of data centers. It says that in Florida, “projections for resource and transmission growth lag behind what is needed to support new data centers and other large loads.” “As of April 2026, eight data centers are planned for construction in Florida,” the order says. OUC’s CEO, Clint Bullock, raised the same concern at a public workshop earlier this month. “The size of these hyperscalers is like nothing we’ve ever seen. You can’t forecast it into your traditional forecasting. That’s why this is a concern,” Bullock said. Hyperscalers are the massive data centers run by companies such as Google and Amazon. OUC says data centers are only part of the picture. The utility points to faster-than-expected growth in electric vehicles, more manufacturing, and a lack of new power generation across Florida. “There hasn’t been a whole lot of new generation that has been built in the last several years,” Alancastro said. Recent winter and summer weather events have also increased peak energy demand. As a result, OUC is increasing its reserve margin from 15% to 20% to help ensure reliable service during periods of high demand. At the workshop, OUC proposed its Electric Integrated Resource Plan, a 20-year roadmap, which does not take coal off the table. The workshop presentation is posted on OUCFuturePlanning.com. Under the plan, Stanton Unit 1 comes back online in 2028, converted so it can run on either coal or natural gas. Stanton Unit 2 gets the same conversion in 2029. The plan does not set an end date for burning coal at Stanton. “It leverages existing infrastructure. The cost to convert those units are far more economical than building a new resource,” Alancastro said. The plan also adds 150 megawatts of solar and 100 megawatts of battery storage by 2035. A gas plant with carbon capture and 345 megawatts of nuclear power are penciled in for the 2040s. Castro described those as placeholders that could change as technology develops. OUC says the plan still meets its goals of cutting carbon emissions 50% by 2030 and 75% by 2040, compared with 2005 levels. Coal’s share has already shrunk. According to OUC, coal made up 41% of its generating capacity in 2019 and 27% in 2025. Solar grew from less than 1% to 11% over the same period. What it means for your bill OUC says the plan would raise bills by about 1% a year for the next 5 years. There is some short-term relief. OUC is proposing a fuel charge cut that would lower a typical residential bill, based on 1,000 kilowatt-hours a month, by about $5 starting in April 2027. Avalon Park resident Jenna Egensteiner said she supports cleaner energy but wants the details. “Cleaner energy is obviously where you want to go. It’s just how, when, how much, for what,” she said. How to weigh in OUC is taking public comments on the plan through Dec. 4 at oucfutureplanning.com. The OUC board is scheduled to vote on the plan and the proposed fuel cut on Dec. 15.

artigo.texto: Sines perde projeto de hidrogénio da Iberdrola, mas ganha centro de dados da Fortitude Sociedade de capital de risco fundada por António Esteves entra em Sines com projeto de centro de dados, com 202 megawatts. - 2 - ... A lista de investimentos de mais de 24,3 mil milhões previstos para Sines sofreu alterações este ano, avança, esta segunda-feira, o Expresso, dando conta da saída da Iberdrola, que desistiu do seu projeto, avaliado em 426 milhões de euros para produzir hidrogénio verde em Portugal, A informação foi confirmada pela Aicep Global Parques (AGP), entidade responsável por gerir os 3306 hectares da Zona Industrial e Logística de Sines (ZILS). Segundo o jornal, além de uma saída houve também uma entrada, estando a Fortitude Capital, fundada em 2022, por António Esteves, no âmbito de um projeto designado "Hermes" a desenvolver um 'campus' de raiz de centros de dados para inteligência artificial, com 202 megawatts.

artigo.texto: Novas barreiras regulatórias estabelecidas pelos Estados Unidos para a exportação de semicondutores avançados voltados à inteligência artificial reconfiguram o panorama operacional do setor no Brasil, segundo avaliação apresentada pela Keraunos Compute em novembro de 2026. A companhia latino-americana, focada em arquiteturas de computação de alto desempenho, aponta que as medidas externas afetam diretamente os cronogramas de expansão de centros de processamento de dados e pressionam o custo de implementação de novos complexos tecnológicos no território nacional. De acordo com a análise corporativa, a dependência estrutural em relação a componentes importados coloca as empresas locais em uma posição de vulnerabilidade estratégica. A limitação no fornecimento de aceleradores gráficos e processadores neurais de última geração interfere não apenas nas previsões de capacidade computacional instalada, mas também na competitividade do ecossistema doméstico frente a polos consolidados na América do Norte, Europa e Ásia. Dependência externa e sensibilidade da infraestrutura digital A cadeia de suprimentos de componentes de alta performance opera sob forte concentração geográfica, mantendo o mercado brasileiro atrelado a diretrizes de controle comercial formuladas em Washington. Conforme as alegações da Keraunos Compute, o endurecimento das regras de exportação atinge o mercado em um período de aceleração nas demandas por treinamento de modelos de linguagem e processamento massivo de dados corporativos. Historicamente, o setor nacional de tecnologia da informação absorve equipamentos com tributação elevada e logística complexa. A inclusão de restrições geopolíticas introduz barreiras não tarifárias adicionais, capazes de desacelerar investimentos de hyperscalers e operadores regionais que planejavam aportes em solo brasileiro para atender à demanda de processamento de baixa latência na América do Sul. Matriz de impacto operacional nos centros de processamento As consequências práticas das limitações de fornecimento se manifestam em múltiplas etapas da estruturação de ativos computacionais. O encarecimento das unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs) e a escassez de opções homologadas geram distorções imediatas no orçamento de bens de capital (Capex) e nos custos de manutenção e atualização de sistemas (Opex). O quadro analítico sintetiza os vetores críticos destacados pela entidade ao mensurar os gargalos enfrentados por investidores. A necessidade de recorrer a rotas intermediárias de distribuição ou a modelos de hardware com capacidade rebaixada compromete a eficiência energética das instalações, parâmetro decisivo na rentabilidade dos empreendimentos modernos. Soberania de dados e reformulação de arquiteturas computacionais A discussão técnica levantada pela entidade transcende a disponibilidade de componentes eletrônicos e alcança a governança informacional. O conceito de infraestrutura soberana de inteligência artificial ganha relevância quando restrições unilaterais limitam a capacidade de governos e corporações locais processarem informações estratégicas dentro de suas próprias fronteiras. Para a fornecedora especializada, a retenção de dados sensíveis em jurisdições nacionais demanda clusters locais robustos, imunes a descontinuidades de fornecimento ou bloqueios repentinos. Sem a garantia de reposição e expansão dos parques de hardware, a prestação de serviços essenciais baseados em inteligência artificial corre o risco de sofrer descontinuidade ou perda de performance comparativa. Os desdobramentos técnicos incluem alterações mandatórias nas estratégias de desenvolvimento de software e gerenciamento de hardware: - Otimização algorítmica voltada a hardware de gerações anteriores, visando extrair maior rendimento de infraestruturas legadas; - Migração de cargas de trabalho críticas para arquiteturas computacionais híbridas e modulares; - Diversificação de fornecedores globais de microeletrônica para diminuir o vínculo com designs exclusivos controlados por licenças restritivas; - Ampliação de centros de pesquisa voltados ao desenvolvimento de soluções abertas de orquestração de servidores. Dinâmica de custos de capital e atratividade de investimentos O volume de investimentos direcionado a data centers no Brasil é pautado pela disponibilidade de energia renovável, infraestrutura de conectividade por cabos submarinos e estabilidade institucional. Contudo, a empresa adverte que a incerteza quanto à importação de equipamentos essenciais pode reordenar a prioridade de fundos internacionais de infraestrutura. A elevação do risco regulatório encarece o financiamento de grandes complexos industriais de processamento. Projetos projetados para consumir dezenas de megawatts dependem da entrega tempestiva de milhares de processadores especializados para justificar os desembolsos de engenharia civil e de subestações de energia já executados. A Keraunos Compute argumenta que operadores de data centers colocation e provedores de serviços gerenciados podem repassar os custos adicionais de importação e compliance para os contratos de serviços em nuvem. Esse movimento inflaciona a digitalização de médias e grandes empresas brasileiras, que dependem do processamento escalável para manter sua eficiência mercadológica. Perspectivas para a cadeia de valor tecnológico regional Diante do quadro imposto por determinações geopolíticas de potências estrangeiras, analistas do setor observam a urgência de respostas coordenadas entre o setor produtivo e formuladores de políticas públicas. A viabilização de regimes aduaneiros facilitados para componentes de computação avançada e o estímulo à atração de centros de design de circuitos integrados emergem como contramedidas discutidas por entidades industriais. A busca por fornecedores alternativos de semicondutores fora do circuito tradicional sujeito às restrições norte-americanas também desponta no planejamento de longo prazo de companhias que atuam no segmento latino-a

artigo.texto: Ola Electric is betting that manufacturing its own battery cells can give it a lasting cost advantage in India's electric two-wheeler market. The company has commissioned 6 GWh of cell manufacturing capacity at its Gigafactory and is now working to improve production yields before integrating these cells into its vehicles. If the ramp-up succeeds, the investment could reduce its dependence on external suppliers, lower battery costs and improve the economics of its automotive business. However, the benefits will depend on how quickly production becomes efficient and whether the company can utilise the capacity at scale. With a market capitalization of Rs. 16,285.70 crore, the shares of Ola Electric Mobility Ltd were trading at Rs. 32.58 per share, down 0.94 percent from its previous closing price of Rs. 32.89 apiece. The 6 GWh Gigafactory moves Ola closer to battery integration Ola Electric has commissioned 6 GWh of cell manufacturing capacity, with commercial operations beginning in September 2026. This is an important step in its strategy to bring more of the electric vehicle supply chain in-house. Battery cells are among the most important cost components of an electric vehicle. Manufacturing them internally could give Ola greater control over procurement, product design and supply availability. It may also reduce its exposure to external suppliers as production volumes increase. However, commissioning capacity does not automatically translate into lower costs. The facility must achieve stable yields, consistent quality and sufficient utilisation before it can deliver meaningful savings. The cell business also remains small relative to the automotive business, with Q2 FY27 revenue of just Rs.3 crore and an adjusted operating EBITDA loss of Rs.38 crore. Cell yields will determine whether manufacturing becomes economical The biggest near-term challenge is improving manufacturing efficiency. Ola currently reports NMC cell yields of around 70–75%, meaning a portion of production does not meet the required quality standards. Management is targeting yields of 80–85% by the end of Q3 FY27 and approximately 90% by Q4 FY27. These targets are important because higher yields allow more usable cells to be produced from the same quantity of raw materials, improving manufacturing economics. Management expects that at around 70% yield, producing cells internally can reach cost parity with buying them externally. At 85% yield, it expects a 10–15% saving at the cell gross-margin level compared with external procurement. However, this is not the same as a 10–15% improvement in the automotive segment's overall margins. The benefit must first offset manufacturing expenses and translate into lower battery costs for the vehicle business. Until yields improve and production stabilises, the expected savings remain a management target rather than an established advantage. Captive demand could provide the initial scale Ola's automotive business is expected to be the first major customer for its cell manufacturing facility. Management estimates that the vehicle business could consume around 2–3 GWh of cells in FY28. Based on management's assumption of an average 5 kWh battery per vehicle, this requirement would correspond to approximately 4–5 lakh vehicles. This level of captive demand could help the cell business achieve an important utilisation threshold. Management expects the cell business's fixed and operating costs to break even against the economics of purchasing cells externally at consumption of around 2–3 GWh. This makes automotive volumes important not only for revenue growth but also for the economics of the Gigafactory. However, the company must first demonstrate that it can consistently manufacture enough usable cells while maintaining quality. If vehicle demand or production falls short of expectations, lower utilisation could delay the benefits of vertical integration. LFP cells and Gen 4 could further reduce vehicle costs Ola is also preparing to introduce lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells alongside its existing nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) technology. Management expects LFP production to ramp up during Q2/Q3 FY27, with yields reaching around 70% by Q4 FY27 and approximately 90% by Q1 FY28. From Q4 FY27 onwards, the company plans to integrate its own LFP cells into vehicles, with a targeted product mix of approximately 30% NMC and 70% LFP. The company also expects its Gen 4 platform, planned from Q4 FY27, to support further reductions in the bill of materials. These changes could improve vehicle cost competitiveness, particularly if Ola can combine lower cell costs with its existing engineering and component-integration capabilities. Management claims that its current bill of materials is already 15–20% lower than competitors despite offering higher functionality and specifications. This is a company claim and has not been independently established in the disclosed figures. The actual benefit will depend on whether the new platform and battery mix deliver savings without compromising performance, reliability or customer demand. External demand could support a larger Gigafactory Ola's longer-term ambition extends beyond supplying its own vehicles. Management is exploring opportunities to sell cells to external original equipment manufacturers and use additional capacity for energy-storage products under its Shakti business. The company has indicated that it could eventually expand the facility from 6 GWh to 20 GWh. Management estimates that capital expenditure per GWh could be below Rs.400 crore at a fully utilised 20 GWh facility, partly because the existing infrastructure has been designed to accommodate expansion. However, this expansion is not immediate. Management has prioritised stabilising the existing 6 GWh capacity before committing to a larger facility. artigo.texto: Denza Z9GT: conheça a perua elétrica de luxo de 1.156 cv em impressões ao volante Denza Z9GT combina três motores elétricos, 1.156 cv e tecnologia de luxo em uma perua que acelera de 0 a 100 km/h em 2,7 segundos. Crédito: Estadão Com apenas duas rodas apoiadas no asfalto, o Denza B5 movimentou um avião Boeing 747-400 de aproximadamente 180 toneladas no aeródromo de Dunsfold, em Surrey, no Reino Unido. A marca de luxo da BYD promoveu o desafio extremo para testar os limites SUV híbrido. A aeronave escolhida para a demonstração, aposentada em 2020, mantém os motores e o interior completo. Isso significa que sua massa equivale a cerca de 72 vezes a capacidade nominal de reboque do utilitário esportivo, declarada em 2.500 kg. Leia também - Cadillac Escalade V8: dirigimos o SUV queridinho das estrelas que a GM promete ao Brasil - Chevrolet Celta e BYD Yuan Plus: veja os carros usados que vendem mais rápido no Brasil - Depois de 1,3 milhão de multas canceladas, free flow volta a punir quem não paga o pedágio Para superar essa diferença de peso sem modificações no trem de força original, o modelo contou com toda a entrega do conjunto de fábrica. A motorização combina um propulsor 1.5 turbo a gasolina — que atua apenas como gerador durante o reboque — a três motores elétricos (dois para tração, um em cada eixo) e à bateria Blade LFP de 31,8 kWh, gerando 544 cv e 77,4 kgfm de torque. Por sua vez, a operação sobre apenas um lado do veículo exigiu adaptações estruturais pontuais para garantir aderência e equilíbrio dinâmico, com o teste dividido em três etapas: - Primeira arrancada: o SUV puxou o avião na configuração padrão, utilizando as quatro rodas. - Segunda tentativa: os engenheiros retiraram uma das rodas e adicionaram 2.000 kg de lastro interno. - Fase final: a equipe removeu outro pneu (deixando apenas o lado esquerdo no chão) e instalou estabilizadores nos eixos, engate sob medida e 4.500 kg de peso extra no lugar dos bancos traseiros. Somando as três passagens, o Denza B5 percorreu 1.600 metros com o avião engatado e precisou aguardar o asfalto secar parcialmente após uma chuva forte nas tentativas finais. Quem assumiu o volante foi Mark Gallifant, técnico sênior da BYD no Reino Unido, superando seu recorde anterior ao rebocar um ônibus de dois andares lotado. De acordo com a fabricante, o feito garante dois recordes inéditos: é o primeiro carro de produção a rebocar um avião sobre duas rodas e o primeiro a deslocar um Boeing 747 usando exclusivamente energia elétrica. Após os percursos, as vistorias técnicas não apontaram desgaste estrutural no chassi, nos pneus ou no trem de força, indica a empresa. Denza no mercado brasileiro Para atrair visibilidade para seus carros e tecnologias, a BYD tem estabelecido desafios públicos com seus carros - o que a fez, por exemplo, quebrar um recorde de velocidade recentemente. No Brasil, a Denza especificamente tem conquistado mercado no segmennto premium. Em outubro de 2026, o B5 fechou o quinto mês consecutivo na liderança dos SUVs de luxo no país, somando 577 unidades emplacadas contra 405 do BMW X1. No acumulado de janeiro a outubro de 2026, o modelo da BYD chegou a 3.777 registros. O ritmo de vendas reduziu para apenas 172 unidades a vantagem do rival alemão, que acumula 3.949 emplacamentos na disputa anual da categoria. Carregando ofertas...

artigo.texto: Lauro Jardim Informações exclusivas sobre política, economia, negócios, esporte, cultura. Brasil concentra 1/4 das reservas mundiais de grafite, essencial para baterias, mas... Prestes a realizar os primeiros leilões de baterias, no início de dezembro, o Brasil concentra 24% das reservas mundiais de grafite, mineral essencial para a fabricação dos produtos, mas responde por apenas 3% da produção global. Das quase 98 mil famílias de patentes analisadas pelo Instituto E+ Transição Energética, só 36 são brasileiras, o equivalente a 0,04%, enquanto a China concentra 57,8%. artigo.texto: BYD is making its presence felt as much as possible just about everywhere, including the Land Down Under. They say that models like the Sealion 7 benefit the people who need them the most, including in rural areas; they joined forces earlier this month with the AFL (Australian Football League) by signing a major partnership with the Hawthorn Football Club, and back in October already celebrated 150k unit sales in the region. As far as models are concerned, BYD made available in September the smaller ATTO 2 DM-i featuring the Dual Mode 4.0 Super Hybrid platform and the Blade battery using Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) chemistry, as well as the ATTO 3 featuring the new e-Platform 3.0 EV architecture with 800 volts. Now it’s time for a proper flagship of the people mover variety – the company first confirmed the all-new BYD M9 minivan was coming to Australia back in August and then announced the pricing configuration in September, with the model starting from AU $61,990 for the base eight-seat M9 Dynamic model and from AU $72,990 (over $48k) sans OTR for the seven-seat M9 Premium variant. The Chinese brand now announces the arrival of the BYD M9 on the market, with BYD's first new energy people mover bringing together the “brand's expertise in new energy vehicle mobility with the versatility Australians expect from large and well-appointed mobility.” Initially, the first version touching down in the Land Down Under is the top-spec seven-seat Premium grade, featuring a 2+2+3 configuration with luxurious leather-appointed and second-row captain’s chairs, a 15.6-inch rear entertainment screen and a 12-speaker audio system among the highlights. The more versatile eight-seat M9 Dynamic featuring a 2+3+3 seating arrangement will come before the end of the year, and both share the latest DM-i Dual Mode 5.0 Super Hybrid system, three-zone air-conditioning, and 470 liters (16.59 cu. Ft.) for luggage with all seats raised. With the rear seats folded, the M9 has 2,036 liters of space – or 71.9 cubic feet of storage. The Dynamic grade has Frequency Selective Damping technology, while the Premium gets BYD's DiSus-C Intelligent Damping Body Control system, but the intelligent plug-in hybrid system is common to both. It consists of a 1.5-liter turbocharged Xiaoyun gasoline engine and a permanent magnet synchronous electric motor with a combined output of 191kW for Dynamic and 218kW for Premium – that’s 256 hp or 292 horsepower. The Dynamic features a 20.4kWh BYD Blade Battery offering up to 80 km of pure electric range or 50 miles, while the Premium version is even more capable thanks to its larger 36.6kWh battery – EV range soars to 145 km or 90 miles. Total combined range is 790km and 850km, respectively, based on WLTP – or 491 and 528 miles, respectively. Both the M9 Dynamic and Premium are solely available with front-wheel drive, though, and feature three intelligent operating modes: EV Pure Electric, HEV Series, where the gasoline engine only acts as a power generator, and HEV Parallel, where both the gasoline and electric motor work together. Inside, BYD gives the driver a 12.3-inch digital instrument display and a 15.6-inch infotainment touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

artigo.texto: Portugal e mais sete países da UE exigem entrada em vigor sem atrasos de novo mercado de carbono - Portugal e outros sete Estados-membros defenderam a entrada em vigor do mercado de carbono europeu sobre emissões de edifícios e transporte rodoviário, sem atrasos. - Numa carta ao comissário europeu do Clima, Wopke Hoekstra, os ministros do Ambiente de vários países manifestaram forte apoio ao CELE 2. - O CELE 2, criado em 2023, é crucial para a descarbonização e segurança energética da Europa, reduzindo a dependência de combustíveis fósseis. Conteúdo Este resumo foi criado com recurso a inteligência artificial. Embora esta tecnologia tenha sido concebida para ser útil e precisa, pode conter erros ou não captar todas as nuances importantes do artigo. Feedback Se consideras que o resumo não está claro ou não reflete bem o conteúdo, envia o teu feedback. A tua opinião é importante para ajudar a melhorar esta funcionalidade! Partilhar Numa carta dirigida ao comissário europeu do Clima, Wopke Hoekstra, os ministros do Ambiente da Dinamarca, Finlândia, Alemanha, Luxemburgo, Países Baixos, Portugal, Espanha e Suécia manifestam “forte apoio” ao Sistema de Comércio Europeu de Licenças de Emissão 2 (CELE 2). Portugal e outros sete Estados-membros defenderam hoje a entrada em vigor, sem novos atrasos, do mercado de carbono europeu sobre emissões de edifícios e transporte rodoviário, numa altura em que vários países contestam a aplicação do mecanismo. Numa carta dirigida ao comissário europeu do Clima, Wopke Hoekstra, os ministros do Ambiente da Dinamarca, Finlândia, Alemanha, Luxemburgo, Países Baixos, Portugal, Espanha e Suécia manifestam “forte apoio” ao Sistema de Comércio Europeu de Licenças de Emissão 2 (CELE 2). O CELE 2 é um mercado de carbono complementar ao CELE original. Enquanto o CELE original abrange as emissões da produção de eletricidade e de calor, da indústria pesada, da aviação e do transporte marítimo, o CELE 2 incide sobre novos setores, como as emissões criadas pela utilização de combustíveis em edifícios e no transporte rodoviário. Criado em 2023, o CELE 2 tinha entrada em vigor inicialmente prevista para 2028, mas países mais dependentes dos combustíveis fósseis, como a Itália ou a Polónia, têm apelado a que essa data seja adiada ou que o sistema seja aligeirado. Foi perante esta pressão que, na cimeira do Conselho Europeu de outubro, os líderes da União Europeia (UE) comprometeram-se a avaliar o impacto do CELE 2 antes da sua entrada em vigor em 2028. Na carta hoje dirigida ao comissário europeu do Clima, que partiu da iniciativa da Dinamarca, os oito ministros frisam que o CELE 2 é hoje “mais importante do que nunca”, numa altura em que “a perturbação dos fluxos de energia através do Estreito de Ormuz voltou a expor a vulnerabilidade da Europa”. “É evidente que temos de reduzir a nossa dependência dos combustíveis fósseis importados, de modo a diminuir a nossa exposição às tensões geopolíticas e aos choques de preços, que prejudicam a competitividade europeia, afetam negativamente as empresas e as famílias, colocam em risco a nossa segurança energética e nos tornam vulneráveis a pressões políticas”, defendem. Os ministros consideram, por isso, que, “ao proporcionar um meio economicamente eficiente de acelerar a descarbonização dos setores dos transportes rodoviários e dos edifícios”, o CELE 2 “reforça a segurança energética da Europa, reduzindo a dependência das importações de combustíveis fósseis e promovendo a eletrificação”. “O CELE 2 desempenha, assim, um papel fundamental no reforço da resiliência da Europa e da sua autonomia estratégica aberta”, insistem. Os ministros recordam ainda que o CELE 2 é “parte integrante de um compromisso mais amplo, que procura alcançar um equilíbrio delicado entre ambição, eficiência em termos de custos e solidariedade”. Dirigindo-se ao comissário europeu do Clima, os ministros manifestam-se “disponíveis para trabalhar de forma construtiva com a Comissão”, para garantir que o CELE 2 entra em vigor “em conformidade com o calendário já acordado”.

artigo.texto: - Power - 2 min read Battery price rebound, rupee fall threaten viability of India’s BESS projects: ICRA The rating agency flags procurement costs, currency movements and execution delays as key risks despite policy support and a growing tender pipeline. India's rapidly expanding battery energy storage system (BESS) market is facing fresh financial viability challenges as a rebound in battery prices, rupee depreciation and aggressive project bidding put pressure on developers' returns, according to a report by rating agency ICRA. While strong policy support and a growing tender pipeline are driving the sector's expansion, the ability of developers to procure batteries at competitive prices and execute projects within stipulated timelines will remain critical to their financial sustainability, ICRA said in its November 2026 report on the Indian renewable energy sector. ICRA's sensitivity analysis indicates that at a battery pack cost of $70 per kWh, BESS projects would generate a cumulative debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) of 1.17-1.27 times at capacity tariffs of ₹2.60-2.80 lakh per MW per month. The DSCR measures a project's ability to generate sufficient cash flows to meet its debt repayment obligations. A relatively narrow coverage margin could leave developers with limited financial flexibility if battery procurement costs rise further or project execution faces delays. Battery procurement costs and currency movements have emerged as key variables determining the viability of aggressively bid projects, the rating agency said, underlining the importance of competitive procurement strategies and protection against cost escalation. ICRA also highlighted the need for robust long-term service agreements (LTSAs) and firm offtake arrangements to safeguard project economics. The concerns come as India's battery storage market moves from the tendering stage towards actual project execution. Rising renewable energy capacity, which continues to outpace transmission augmentation, particularly in resource-rich states such as Rajasthan and Gujarat, is increasing grid congestion and the need for storage infrastructure. Battery storage systems are expected to play a crucial role in absorbing surplus renewable generation during solar hours and shifting electricity supply to periods when solar generation declines. Government support through viability gap funding (VGF) schemes announced in 2023, 2025 and 2026, covering a cumulative 135.8 GWh of storage capacity, is providing significant capital support to the sector. However, policy incentives and lower initial funding requirements alone may not eliminate the financial and operational risks associated with BESS projects. ICRA cautioned that developers also need to account for eventual duty payments under the MOOWR scheme, performance penalties, additional battery requirements and post-warranty maintenance expenses. These costs may not necessarily be covered by supplier guarantees. The rating agency said project assessments should examine whether supplier guarantees adequately cover developers' commitments to power buyers, particularly in cases where equipment performance falls short of contractual requirements. With battery costs, currency movements and execution timelines becoming increasingly important to project economics, timely procurement and adequate financial safeguards will be crucial for developers navigating India's expanding energy storage market.

With a sea of advantages. We can truly say this offers a glimpse into the future of electric boating. Among the innovations presented at Metstrade 2026 in Amsterdam, we saw a product that aims to revolutionize the world of marine propulsion. It is the Svenner II from EPT Technologies, the first solid-state marine battery to receive DNV certification. A solution that combines four features of particular interest to boaters: certification, high fire safety, long service life, and constant monitoring. The Svenner II battery from EPT Technologies The first thing that sets the Svenner II apart is its DNV certification, a major milestone for the marine battery industry. This certification confirms the battery’s compliance with rigorous safety and reliability requirements and offers benefits not only to shipyards and system integrators—who can rely on a pre-certified system—but also to boat owners seeking reliable solutions for onboard electrification. The battery is designed for use on various types of vessels, including both sailboats and motorboats. Greater Fire Safety The second advantage concerns one of the most sensitive issues when it comes to onboard batteries: the risk of fire. Svenner II uses solid-state technology that replaces most of the liquid electrolytes in traditional batteries with solid materials. This approach increases the thermal stability of the cells and significantly reduces the risk of uncontrolled reactions. The cells have passed particularly rigorous tests, including multiple overload and puncture tests, without generating heat or triggering thermal runaway. Furthermore, in the event of an accident, the DNV-certified solution allows the incident to be contained within a single module, limiting the impact on the rest of the battery pack. Over 10,000 life cycles The third key strength is longevity. Svenner II claims a service life of over 10,000 cycles, based on a depth of discharge (DoD) of 80%. By comparison, traditional lithium batteries average around 4,000–5,000 cycles. This means you can count on more than double the operational lifespan, with fewer replacements over the years and the potential to reduce overall operating costs. Integrated sensors and continuous monitoring The fourth advantage is monitoring of operating conditions. Svenner II integrates a system The BMS features a dual-core CPU in a lockstep configuration, which ensures redundancy and continuous operational monitoring. The battery pack also includes sensors to detect any water ingress and HVIL interlocks, designed to enhance module protection and monitor safety conditions. The system is also designed to operate in high-temperature environments, an important feature in the most demanding marine installations. artigo.texto: Mercado global de compostos de borracha butílica (IIR): Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de compostos de borracha butílica (IIR) até 2035, impulsionada pela demanda de embalagens farmacêuticas e armazenamento de energia Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de compostos de borracha butílica (IIR), o mercado chega a 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de compostos de borracha butílica (IIR) entra em uma fase de expansão constante, com a demanda projetada para crescer a uma taxa anual composta de 4–6% entre 2026 e 2035. Esse crescimento se apoia nas propriedades singulares de baixa permeabilidade e amortecimento da borracha de isobutileno-isopreno, que a tornam indispensável para vedações de recipientes farmacêuticos, revestimentos internos de pneus e um conjunto cada vez maior de aplicações de armazenamento de energia. As formulações de alta pureza e de especialidade, que representam uma parcela estimada de 25–35% do consumo global em volume, alcançam prêmios de preço de 30–50% e vêm redesenhando os polos de valor ao longo da cadeia de suprimentos. A oferta permanece concentrada em menos de dez produtores globais, com excesso de capacidade nos graus padrão convivendo com a disponibilidade restrita de compostos certificados para uso farmacêutico. A harmonização regulatória em torno da ISO 15378 e da ICH Q7 eleva as barreiras de conformidade e, na prática, consolida a base de fornecedores certificados. Ao mesmo tempo, a Ásia-Pacífico desponta como o centro de demanda de crescimento mais rápido, sustentado pela fabricação farmacêutica por contrato e pela produção de separadores de baterias. Este relatório oferece uma visão baseada em dados sobre tamanho de mercado, segmentação, fluxos comerciais, lógica de precificação e posicionamento competitivo até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado mundial de compostos de borracha butílica (IIR) projeta uma taxa de crescimento anual composta de 4–6% entre 2026 e 2035, com o índice de mercado subindo de 100 em 2025 para cerca de 155 em 2035. Espera-se que o crescimento seja desigual entre os segmentos: os compostos de IIR de grau padrão enfrentam pressão sobre as margens decorrente da volatilidade das matérias-primas e do excesso de capacidade, enquanto as formulações de alta pureza e de especialidade tendem a se expandir acima da média à medida que os clientes dos setores farmacêutico e de armazenamento de energia ampliam suas operações. A concentração da oferta em um pequeno grupo de produtores globais continua sendo uma característica estrutural, e é provável que os acréscimos de capacidade para material certificado de grau farmacêutico fiquem aquém da demanda, sustentando os prêmios de preço. Espera-se que os fluxos comerciais se desloquem para a Ásia-Pacífico, onde a fabricação por contrato e a produção de separadores de baterias avançam rapidamente. Entre os riscos de baixa estão oscilações superiores a 20% em um ano nos preços das matérias-primas petroquímicas e ciclos prolongados de qualificação de fornecedores, de 12 a 24 meses, que limitam a flexibilidade dos compradores. O potencial de alta reside na adoção mais rápida de compostos de IIR em formatos emergentes de armazenamento de energia e na contínua substituição, induzida por exigências regulatórias, por graus certificados de alta pureza. Vetores e restrições da demanda Principais vetores de demanda - Demanda sustentada por elastômeros de baixa permeabilidade em vedações e fechamentos de recipientes farmacêuticos, apoiada pela harmonização regulatória em torno da ISO 15378 e da ICH Q7. - Aplicações emergentes de armazenamento de energia, incluindo a produção de separadores de baterias, que exigem compostos de IIR de alta pureza com perfis rigorosos de extraíveis e lixiviáveis. - Crescimento da demanda por revestimentos internos de pneus, sobretudo na Ásia-Pacífico, onde a produção de veículos e os gastos em infraestrutura seguem robustos. - Migração para masterbatches de IIR pré-compostos e específicos para cada cliente, que encurtam os ciclos de qualificação e ampliam a captura de valor pelos formuladores. - Exigências crescentes de conformidade para graus de alta pureza, que consolidam a base de fornecimento certificada e sustentam preços premium. - Expansão da fabricação farmacêutica por contrato na Ásia-Pacífico, impulsionando o crescimento do consumo regional. Possíveis restrições ao crescimento - Volatilidade dos custos de matérias-primas, especialmente do isobutileno derivado de correntes petroquímicas de C4, com oscilações de preço à vista superiores a 20% em um ano. - Ciclos longos de qualificação de fornecedores, de 12 a 24 meses, para compostos de IIR de grau farmacêutico, o que limita a flexibilidade dos compradores e retarda a adoção. - Excesso de capacidade nos graus padrão, que comprime as margens dos compostos e desestimula investimentos em nova capacidade. - Gargalos de capacidade para IIR de alta pureza, já que as linhas existentes, originalmente projetadas para borracha butílica de grau para pneus, exigem investimentos significativos em acabamento em sala limpa e sistemas de qualidade validados. Estrutura da demanda por setor de uso final Embalagens farmacêuticas e vedações de recipientes (participação estimada: 28%) As vedações de recipientes farmacêuticos representam o uso final de maior intensidade de valor para os compostos de borracha butílica (IIR), com demanda impulsionada pela necessidade de elastômeros de baixa permeabilidade e quimicamente inertes que preservem a estabilidade dos medicamentos. artigo.texto: American Battery Technology has seen its share price slide sharply in recent years, which naturally pushes investors to ask whether the current valuation is still supported by the company’s sales. With the stock now trading at around US$0.79, the key issue is how that market value lines up with what the business is actually generating in revenue. Over the past 5 years the share price has fallen 95.9%, which puts intense focus on whether the revenue base can justify even today’s much lower level. The business model depends on turning battery materials technology into consistent commercial sales, so investors are watching how quickly those projects can translate into stable top line revenue and cash generation. The issue now is whether the stock’s current price is well supported by American Battery Technology’s sales when measured against the Fair Ratio benchmark. Has American Battery Technology Run Too Far on Sales? P/S is usually the cleaner yardstick for a company like American Battery Technology that is still reporting losses, because it compares the share price with the revenue it already books rather than profits that are not yet there. On this measure, American Battery Technology trades on a P/S of about 5.0x, which is almost identical to the peer group near 5.0x and more than double the wider metals and mining sector at roughly 2.2x. The Fair Ratio model, which blends factors such as the firm’s growth profile, margins, size and risk, flags that this current multiple screens as overvalued and suggests the penalty for ongoing losses and execution risk is steep. The gap is so wide that the Fair Ratio output is better read as a warning sign that the stock prices its revenue stream very expensively on this framework, rather than a precise fair value estimate. artigo.texto: UPCL Invites Bids for 41 MW/102.5 MWh Battery Storage Projects 23 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Uttarakhand Power Corporation has invited bids to establish 41 MW/102.5 MWh of grid-interactive standalone Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) across six 33/11 kV substations in Uttarakhand. The projects will be developed under the Build-Own-Operate model through capacity charge-based competitive bidding, with Viability Gap Funding (VGF) support of up to Rs. 1.8 mn per MWh. The tender, numbered CCP-I/49/2026-2027, was issued on November 17, 2026. The pre-bid meeting is scheduled for November 26 at 11:30 am at UPCL’s Dehradun office, with online participation available. Bidders must submit queries by 5 pm on the same day through the designated tender email address. The combined capacity will be distributed across substations in Uttarkashi, Haridwar and Tehri districts. The identified locations are Kalyani and Dhanarigaad in Uttarkashi, SIDCUL Sector 8 and Jwalapur 2 in Haridwar, New Manglaur in Roorkee, and Rajakhet in Tehri. Individual project capacities range from 4 MW/10 MWh to 10 MW/25 MWh. Selected systems must complete two charge-discharge cycles daily. Each cycle will include 2.5 hours of discharge during the morning peak and another 2.5 hours during the evening peak. UPCL will provide land at its substations to successful developers under a Right of Use arrangement. The VGF assistance will be provided as non-recurring financial support and funded entirely by the central government. Developers will handle design, financing, supply, installation, commissioning, operations and maintenance. Projects must be commissioned within 12 months of the later of the effective date of the Battery Energy Storage Purchase Agreement (BESPA) or land handover, while the BESPA will run for 12 years after full commissioning. The tender requires an earnest money deposit of Rs. 41.3 mn, while the bid submission and opening schedules are set out in the Notice Inviting Tender. artigo.texto: Balmer Lawrie Invites Bids for 522 kWh BESS and Solar Project 23 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Balmer Lawrie & Co. has invited online bids to establish a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) integrated with a 600 kW solar power plant at its industrial packaging facility in Taloja, Navi Mumbai. The contract covers the supply, installation, testing and commissioning of a 522 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery storage system. The proposed BESS will store surplus electricity generated during daylight hours and supply it during the evening and periods of peak demand. The project is intended to improve solar power utilisation and strengthen energy management at the facility. The tender has been issued through the company’s e-procurement portal under reference number 0100PC3430. Eligible bidders must be registered entities with an average annual turnover of at least Rs. 9 mn during the financial years 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. They must also demonstrate experience in solar power execution, including at least one grid-connected solar installation with a capacity of 300 kW or higher. Bidders must be based in Mumbai or within approximately 200 km by road, maintain an office or authorised service centre in Maharashtra and hold a valid state electrical contractor licence. A site visit to the Taloja facility is mandatory, with bidders required to submit valid attendance proof. A gate pass alone will not be accepted. No advance payment will be made to the successful bidder. The tender was published on November 17, 2026, and proposals must be submitted by November 27 at 16:00 hours, with opening scheduled for 16:05 hours the same day. The selected bidder must confirm purchase-order acceptance within seven days and complete the project within 10 weeks of site clearance. The tender requires an Earnest Money Deposit of Rs. 45,000, although eligible Micro and Small Enterprises with valid registration are exempt. Security Deposit is set at 3 per cent of the basic order value, while 10 per cent of the total order value will be retained as performance security, subject to the stated release and guarantee conditions. artigo.texto: Juniper Green Commissions 108.50 MWp Solar and 94.77 MWh BESS 23 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Juniper Green Energy has commissioned capacities across two renewable energy projects through its subsidiaries. Juniper Green ETA Five has completed the entire 108.50 MWp solar component of a 75 MW wind-solar hybrid power project, while Juniper Green Stellar has commissioned a 94.77 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). Both commissioning activities took place at their respective project sites on November 19, 2026. The solar component forms part of a project being developed under a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company (MSEDCL). Juniper Green ETA Five, a wholly owned subsidiary of Juniper Green Energy, undertook the commissioning. The company disclosed the development through a regulatory filing. Juniper Green Stellar, another wholly owned subsidiary, commissioned the 94.77 MWh BESS as merchant capacity. The storage facility will initially operate in the merchant market, although the subsidiary retains the option of transferring the capacity to a long-term PPA in the future. Earlier this year, Juniper Green Energy fully commissioned a 100 MWh merchant BESS project at Bikaner in Rajasthan through its subsidiary Juniper Green Cosmic. The project is among the first operational merchant BESS facilities in India. The company also completed a 150 MW wind-solar hybrid project awarded by Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam after commissioning its final 5 MW wind turbine. The 150 MW hybrid project was secured through the greenshoe option under a 500 MW tender issued by Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam. Juniper Green received the project at a tariff of Rs. 3.04/kWh, while KPI Green Energy secured a 50 MW project at Rs. 2.99/kWh. The latest commissioning adds to Juniper Green Energy’s operating renewable generation and storage portfolio. artigo.texto: Data centers: expansÃ£o tecnolÃ³gica esbarra em dilemas econÃ´micos e socioambientais Setor empresarial defende fortalecimento da soberania digital, enquanto pesquisadores e entidades questionam a geraÃ§Ã£o de empregos e os custos socioambientais Publicado: 21/11/2026 Ã s 08:00 Os data centers sÃ£o criticados, entre outros motivos, pelo elevado consumo de energia e Ã¡gua (DIVULGAÃÃO/GOV.BR) A infraestrutura necessária para a expansão tecnológica no Brasil é um dos grandes dilemas atuais que envolvem o poder público, a sociedade civil e o setor empresarial. No centro do debate estão os data centers, conjuntos de equipamentos que funcionam como o “cérebro” físico de toda a rede mundial de computadores. De um lado, apoiadores defendem a criação de empregos e o reforço da soberania digital frente às big techs estrangeiras. Do outro, críticos apontam que os supostos benefícios não compensariam os impactos socioambientais causados. De acordo com a Associação Brasileira de Data Center (ABDC), a expectativa é de que o setor de data centers atraia até R$ 1 trilhão em investimentos até 2036. Os números serão possíveis a partir de políticas de desoneração como o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata), sancionado pelo Governo Federal em setembro deste ano, que prevê a isenção de impostos de importação na aquisição de equipamentos destinados aos data centers. Um relatório da agência de classificação de risco estadunidense Moody’s, divulgado em janeiro deste ano, aponta que o Brasil ocupa o 12º lugar no ranking global de data centers. No contexto da América Latina, o país lidera em número de empreendimentos com quase 200 data centers, metade da quantidade de estruturas em funcionamento na região. A maior parte se concentra na região Sudeste, mais especificamente nos estados de São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro. Em Pernambuco, a instalação de um data center em Paranatama, município com uma população aproximada de 12 mil pessoas no Agreste do estado, chegou a receber a licença da Agência Estadual de Meio Ambiente (CPRH). Porém, a mobilização de entidades da sociedade civil e as mudanças no processo de licenciamento para empreendimentos do tipo aprovadas pelo Conselho Nacional do Meio Ambiente (Conama) fizeram a empresa recuar. A desistência do projeto foi anunciada pelo Ministério Público de Pernambuco (MPPE), no último dia 11 de novembro, em audiência pública convocada para debater o tema. Em um evento de tecnologia no início do mês, a governadora Raquel Lyra ponderou os impactos da atração dos empreendimentos para os recursos naturais do estado, em especial sobre o fornecimento de água. “Lido com o El Niño, com a racionalização da água, e tenho que instalar data center. Tenho um polo cervejeiro, um polo de jeans e vou usar minha água onde? Os recursos são escassos”, afirmou. A gestora também questionou o retorno econômico e a geração de empregos frente ao investimento necessário. Durante a campanha eleitoral deste ano, o tema já havia sido abordado por João Campos, candidato derrotado na corrida pelo Executivo estadual. Em entrevistas e sabatinas, o ex-prefeito do Recife criticou a suposta falta de articulação da gestão atual na atração dos investimentos, citando como exemplo a instalação de um data center da empresa ByteDance, proprietária da plataforma TikTok, no município de Caucaia, na Região Metropolitana de Fortaleza. Geração de empregos e retorno econômico A mão de obra envolvida na instalação de um data center se distribui entre os trabalhadores que executam as obras de construção da infraestrutura física, os postos ocupados durante a operação do empreendimento e outros setores envolvidos de forma secundária nas atividades. De acordo com um levantamento da Fundação Getúlio Vargas (FGV), um único data center de 100 megawatts para operações de inteligência artificial pode envolver um investimento total de R$ 25 bilhões e gerar cerca de 12,5 mil empregos diretos e indiretos, sendo 10,7 mil temporários e 1,8 mil permanentes. Para o advogado André Fernandes, fundador e pesquisador líder do Instituto de Pesquisa em Direito e Tecnologia do Recife (IP.rec), a injeção de vagas no mercado de trabalho não seria suficiente para compensar os impactos socioambientais dos empreendimentos. Ele compara com outros empreendimentos locais, como a Refinaria Abreu e Lima e o Estaleiro Atlântico Sul, que teriam mobilizado uma quantidade maior de trabalhadores nas etapas de edificação. “É uma obra de engenharia civil muito mais simples. A estrutura de construção civil é um galpão de concreto pré-moldado com a instalação de toda uma parafernália elétrica de resfriamento, com ou sem água. Você não tem toda essa geração de emprego. O questionamento que nossos mandantes deveriam fazer é se faz sentido, para economia, o tipo de investimento e as consequências de médio e longo prazo. A nível indireto e direto, são pouquíssimos empregos”, apontou. O professor Abraham Sicsú, doutor em Economia, aponta a necessidade de observar o fenômeno do ponto de vista qualitativo, além de considerar estratégias como o powershoring, que propõe a instalação de empreendimentos de alto consumo energético em regiões com oferta abundante de energias renováveis. “Embora o data center em si não gere muito emprego, com o powershoring e com a cadeia de suprimentos, você passa a ter setores significativamente empregantes e com emprego mais qualificado, mais tecnificado e com melhores salários. Então melhora a qualidade da empregabilidade”, avaliou. Já o presidente do Porto Digital, Pierre Lucena, pondera a necessidade de analisar com cautela a construção dos empreendimentos ligados às big techs, que possuem requisitos diferenciados. “Precisamos distinguir a infraestrutura que atende às empresas locais daquela voltada, principalmente, às demandas de grandes plataformas globais. artigo.texto: Em parceria inédita com a AKAD Seguros e estruturada com a corretora Marsh, a climatech brasileira eleva o padrão de integridade e blindará 100% das suas emissões contra falhas na entrega, riscos de projetos e greenwashing Em um movimento pioneiro para sanar o principal gargalo de confiança do mercado de ativos ambientais, a Greenline, multinacional brasileira de tecnologia climática, anuncia a adoção de apólice de seguro obrigatória para a totalidade dos créditos de carbono mensurados e emitidos em suas operações. A solução foi desenvolvida e estruturada com o apoio da corretora internacional Marsh e comercializada pela AKAD Seguros. A iniciativa responde à crescente exigência de grandes compradores globais por segurança jurídica, financeira e reputacional diante de controvérsias sobre a integridade e a permanência de projetos de conservação florestal. Com a nova política, a Greenline passa a ser a primeira empresa a exigir cobertura securitária como pré-requisito indispensável para a emissão de créditos ex-post, emitidos após verificação dos resultados. O seguro cobrirá quatro frentes críticas de risco que costumam travar grandes transações no mercado voluntário: falha na entrega dos créditos de carbono contratados; falha estrutural do projeto responsável pela geração; perda permanente de utilidade dos ativos, inclusive desqualificação de metodologias ou autorizações governamentais; e custos adicionais para a aquisição de créditos substitutos no mercado caso os ativos originais sofram sinistros ou desqualificação. A apólice prevê ainda a cobertura de despesas emergenciais estratégicas para a mitigação de danos, como custos imediatos com combate a incêndios florestais e realização de auditorias de urgência após desastres naturais. O parâmetro inicial estabelecido é de US$ 25 milhões em limite de cobertura por projeto. Tomando como referência o preço médio de US$ 10 por crédito, cada projeto segurado pela Greenline poderá contar com proteção equivalente a 2,5 milhões de toneladas de gás carbônicos. “Controvérsias sobre a qualidade dos créditos, regularidade fundiária e o risco reputacional do greenwashing tornaram-se tópicos centrais em nossas negociações com grandes compradores corporativos. Tornar o seguro obrigatório em 100% das nossas operações não é apenas uma garantia financeira. É uma declaração de maturidade do setor. Estamos transformando ativos ambientais em instrumentos financeiros verdadeiramente bancáveis“, destaca Lucio Lopez, fundador e CEO da Greenline. Padrão metodológico permite retrospectiva de carteira Além das novas emissões, a cobertura securitária também poderá contemplar projetos que já eram mensurados pela Greenline antes da parceria formal com a AKAD, sujeitos à avaliação de risco da seguradora. A viabilidade dessa extensão decorre da padronização tecnológica e dos rigorosos processos de mensuração via sensoriamento remoto mantidos pela climatech. Desenvolvida focado na preservação de florestas nativas e redução de desmatamento, a solução foi concebida para atender o mercado de forma ampla. A Greenline atuou como articuladora da demanda, mas o produto também estará disponível para outros agentes do setor de ativos ambientais conforme critérios da AKAD. artigo.texto: BYD's Hybrid Slump Sets the Bar for Ti9 as Legal and Brokerage Headwinds Pile Up Published on 11/21/2026 at 17:40 | Editorial boerse-global.de A Dutch court's ruling against the BYD Ti7, two trimmed price targets and a flagship launch meant to plug a hybrid-sized hole — the past few days have handed BYD investors plenty to digest at once. The legal setback came first. A court in the Netherlands ruled yesterday that sales of the Ti7 must stop across the European Union, according to Reuters, after concluding the model infringes the design of Jaguar Land Rover's Defender. BYD shares slipped 3.6% on the session to close at €7.05. Analysts were already moving in the same direction. Daiwa cut its target for BYD's H-shares to HK$100 from HK$119 yesterday while keeping its buy rating, pointing to weaker demand in the company's Chinese home market than it had expected for the final quarter. The brokerage also trimmed its earnings forecasts, by 7% for 2026 and 9% for 2027. Bank of America Securities had gone earlier, lowering its own target to HK$104 from HK$124 on Wednesday, with its buy recommendation left intact. A 200,000-Vehicle Hole in the Hybrid Book The demand softness Daiwa flags is visible most clearly in plug-in hybrids. BYD sold roughly 200,000 fewer plug-in hybrid passenger cars in the first ten months of this year than in the same stretch of 2024. From January through October the company moved just over 1.6 million plug-in hybrids, down from more than 1.8 million a year earlier — a decline of 11%. Sales of new-energy vehicles as a whole fell only about 2% over the period, to some 3.6 million from 3.7 million, so the weakness is concentrated rather than spread evenly across the range. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? October itself offered a brighter picture. BYD reported around 490,000 new-energy vehicle sales for the month, up 11% from roughly 442,000 a year earlier. All of these figures come from the company's monthly release and are unaudited. Even so, the year-to-date shortfall stands, and it is steepest in hybrids. Fang Cheng Bao's Flagship Arrives That is the gap the Ti9 is driving into. Fang Cheng Bao, BYD's group brand, announced the launch date of 19 November via its Weibo account on 17 November, with reservations in China open since 9 November, as Sina Auto reported at the time. The Ti9 is the brand's flagship and sits on BYD's DMS hybrid platform, placing it squarely in the segment that is struggling. One model at the top of a brand will hardly erase a shortfall of about 200,000 vehicles on its own. It does not have to, either, to give the hybrid business a meaningful lift. Why the Shortfall Is No Benchmark Spread across ten months, the gap works out to just over 20,000 vehicles a month. Treating that figure as a hurdle for the Ti9 would be a mistake: it describes what BYD has on average been missing so far, not how many extra hybrids the group must sell each month going forward. That depends on how the rest of the hybrid line-up performs — and on how many Ti9s Fang Cheng Bao actually delivers. The number is a backward-looking average and says nothing about sales of the new model. BYD at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Separately, BYD Battery and Beijing Bus Media signed a memorandum of understanding yesterday covering battery management across the full life cycle, vehicle sales and related services, as well as advertising and brand promotion. The picture is thus clearer than it first appears, though only halfway. Hybrids are the group's weak spot, and the Ti9 is aimed precisely there. How much it can fix will be settled by its unit sales and by the trajectory of the other hybrid models — not by a historical shortfall. artigo.texto: Utica Common Council discusses BESS legislation at committee meeting Alexis Manore | Staff writer | AManore@RNYmedia.com Alexis Manore Staff writer Author facebook Author linkedin Author twitter Author email Nov 24, 2026 5 hrs ago 0 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Utica City Hall Sentinel photo by John Clifford Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save UTICA — The Utica Common Council discussed proposed legislation to regulate battery energy storage systems (BESS) at a Monday, Nov. 23 Committee of the Whole meeting. The council currently has a moratorium on BESS in Utica, having passed several extensions, with the most recent extension set to expire Saturday, Dec. 5. The council’s next regular meeting is Wednesday, Dec. 2. At the Nov. 23 meeting, the councilors reviewed legislation that Assistant Corporation Counsel Stephanie DiGiorgio prepared. The legislation split BESS into three tiers: one for smaller systems that would be allowed, one for larger systems that would require site plan approval from the Planning Board, and the third for large-scale systems, which would only be allowed in industrial and mixed-use industrial zones, and would require a special use permit. After discussion, the councilors decided that large-scale systems should not be allowed at all, and talked about further regulating second-tier systems. The councilors decided to call for a special meeting on Monday, Nov. 30 to introduce its BESS legislation, before introducing it at its Dec. 2 meeting. artigo.texto: It’s the Roaring 2020’s for the HPC-AI Data Center Industry, But It Comes with Costs Key Highlights - Overall HPC spending grew nearly 17% in 2025 to more than $70 billion, with cloud usage up nearly 30%. - The combined on-premises and cloud market for HPC and AI-for-science servers is projected to approach $140 billion by 2030. - GPU wait times can exceed 18 months, while rising HBM and DDR5 prices are pushing up system costs. - Dell overtook HPE for the top server market share, with 23.8% compared with HPE’s 20.9%. - Hyperion estimates the quantum computing market reached $1.4 billion in 2025, while 54% of respondents see a chance of a quantum winter. It has been, and will very likely continue to be, the “Roaring 2020's” for the HPC-AI data center industry. But similar to the generally healthy U.S. economy, affordability is a problem. Driven by demand for advanced computing technology, the HPC-AI data center infrastructure industry is generating tremendous growth, according to the latest market update figures released by industry analyst firm Hyperion Research. But with high demand come strains on supply chains that result in higher costs that restrain even higher growth. This is the picture presented this week by Hyperion at their annual breakfast at the SC26 Supercomputing Conference in Chicago. The customary large crowd turned out to hear Hyperion CEO Earl Joseph and colleagues discuss the state of the industry, some sectors of which are expanding at a clip Joseph said has never before been seen. “2025 was an extremely high growth year for the market…,” said Hyperion CEO Earl Joseph of on-premises servers for HPC, AI and data centers. “The first half of this year is growing at 20 percent… This is more than a doubling of historic growth. And then looking at the overall market in addition to servers, the storage, middleware, application services and spending for running HPC and AI for science workloads in the cloud…the market has just grown tremendously.” Among Hyperion’s key findings: - Overall HPC spending grew by just under 17 percent in 2025 reaching a total of more than $70 billion, including nearly 30 percent growth in cloud usage. - Worldwide sales of on-prem for HPC and AI-for-science servers reached $29.4 billion, an increase of nearly 15 percent, with the EMEA region growing by roughly 10 percent. - For the combination of HPC and AI-for-science on-prem servers plus cloud, the overall market is expected to double over the next five years, approaching $140 billion by 2030. - Growth in sales for on-prem servers during the first of this year was approximately 20 percent, and looking out to 2030, Hyperion projects sales to reach nearly $55 billion. Hyperion also disclosed that Dell has taken the top spot for servers from perennial leader HPE, with Dell capturing 23.8 percent market share versus HPE’s 20.9 percent share. HPC-AI Growth Runs Into Supply Chain Reality But these rosy growth figures generate pressure and unmet demands across the HPC-AI technology ecosystem, including processors, solid state drives (SSDs) and memory. For example, while more than 1 million GPUs were installed in 2025 – a roughly 25 percent growth rate over 2024 – there are reported wait times of 18 months or longer for new GPUs, which command higher prices. There also are the well-documented supply chain problems for memory. Hyperion Senior Vice President of Research Bob Sorensen said the rise in memory prices has added significantly to HPC systems pricing. A Hyperion study found that costs for high bandwidth memory (HBM) per gigabyte has increased since 2021 from between $9 and $11.50 to between $13 and $17 this year. Spread across the hundreds or thousands of nodes within a single system results in a powerful multiplier effect. Sorensen also cited prices for DDR5 SDRAM (Double Data Rate 5) synchronous dynamic random-access memory has jumped in price since 2021 by more than 300 percent. He compared pricing for an HPC system of around 600 petaflops ordered in 2023 compared to 2026 and found that system memory costs have increased from $35 million to more than $60 million, contributing to a complete system price of $125 million (up from $100 million four years ago) in which memory comprises 47 percent of total system cost. The AI boom means high demand and good times for memory vendors, but as Sorensen explained, memory is a volatile business. “Memory makers are loath to increase capacity,” he said. “They know the memory market is a boom bust sector…, they know that sooner or later demand is going to turn and they're going to be dealing with overcapacity or under capacity. So we don't see a real solution to this problem, at least for the next few years.” Cloud Adoption Accelerates as Quantum Computing Faces Uncertainty Hyperion also reported that cloud usage is increasing, with 80 percent of their survey respondents across industry, government and academia reporting utilizing cloud for some portion of their HPC and AI-for-science workloads. Hyperion Research Director Mark Nossokoff said industry sectors sites use cloud the most, according to Hyperion, compared with government organizations and academia. Leading factors favoring use of external clouds include the ability to dynamically add or remove resources, to access new hardware that is otherwise unavailable and to run jobs at scales not possible on-prem.
